{
  "subtype": "exploratory_data_analysis",
  "focus_variable": "state_declined",
  "per_column": [
    {
      "name": "asset_type_category",
      "role": "predictor",
      "is_predictor": true,
      "is_interpretable_segmentation": true,
      "rationale": "Well-separated, interpretable categories (laptop, desktop, service, travel_equipment, etc.) that let an explorer segment decline rates by kind of expense—directly serving the 'what kinds of expenses get declined' question."
    },
    {
      "name": "asset_acquisition_context",
      "role": "predictor",
      "is_predictor": true,
      "is_interpretable_segmentation": true,
      "rationale": "Distinct, human-readable categories (auto_generated, manual_registration, procurement, upgrade_maintenance) representing how an expense originated—an external associational dimension plausibly related to decline likelihood."
    },
    {
      "name": "travel_related_marker",
      "role": "predictor",
      "is_predictor": true,
      "is_interpretable_segmentation": true,
      "rationale": "Clean binary flag with a reasonable split (407/93); travel vs. non-travel is an interpretable segmentation that can be compared against decline rates."
    },
    {
      "name": "device_brand",
      "role": "predictor",
      "is_predictor": true,
      "is_interpretable_segmentation": true,
      "rationale": "Interpretable vendor categories with a dominant few plus an 'Other' bucket; allows grouping to see if certain vendors' expenses are declined more, though somewhat tangential to the intent."
    },
    {
      "name": "department_requesting",
      "role": "restatement",
      "is_predictor": false,
      "is_interpretable_segmentation": true,
      "rationale": "The original table already contains a 'department' column; this duplicates the by-department axis the query explicitly asks about rather than adding a new associational variable. Interpretable but essentially a restatement of an existing dimension."
    }
  ],
  "n_predictors": 4,
  "relationship_informativeness": 0.7,
  "rationale": "As a set, the added columns provide several external, well-separated, interpretable segmentation variables (expense/asset type, acquisition context, travel flag, brand) that genuinely open up relationships with the decline outcome and support the 'what kinds of expenses get declined' exploration. Categories are human-readable, not opaque scores, and value distributions are neither near-constant nor overly fine-grained. The main weakness is device_brand being only loosely tied to the intent and department_requesting duplicating the existing department dimension rather than introducing a novel associational axis—the query's 'by department' angle is already covered by the original schema. Overall a solid, mostly informative exploratory set."
}
